chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who brought a pheasant into the Sanctuary, is it permissible for him to take it out? So he said:
"It is a beast of prey, and whatever beast of prey you bring into the Sanctuary as a captive, you may take it out."
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever is compelled to eat game and a dead animal, let him eat the game and pay its ransom, and not eat the dead animal.

key_terms.اَلْحَرَمُ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or Medina), where specific rules apply.
key_terms.سَبُعٌ: Beast of prey or wild animal.
key_terms.فَهْدٌ: A type of wild goat or pheasant, often used as an example of game/beast of prey.
key_terms.يَفْدِيهِ: To pay ransom or compensation for it.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who brings a live animal into the Haram sanctuary?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of wild animals brought into the Haram, establishing that a beast of prey (sab') is considered captive (asir) and thus permissible to remove. Shaykh al-Tusi supplements this with a practical ruling on compulsion (darura), distinguishing between eating game versus carrion, where the former requires fidyah while the latter is generally avoided, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on minimizing ritual impurity during Hajj.
